critique.missing_from_policy_prompt_for_memory: It did not say that a transient finger reading of about 19-25% seen mid-closure (t=64) does not count as a hook grasp when the fingers go on to reach 0% at the next step (t=80) while the gripper stays at table height (0.02-0.03); fingers reaching 0% means nothing is held, so the method is push even if the gripper first descended near the stick and the stick ends up displaced (from [87,171] to [103,130]) as the gripper swept past it. It also did not say that `hook` requires the stick to be explicitly marked as held (and fingers to stay at ~20-25% throughout the drag), and that a stick simply being nudged aside while the cube slides to the target is a push.
